title: Brush the lint out of a Galaxy S24's charging port with a soft toothbrush, without packing it, and wipe it off
keywords: bristles bending into a 0.93 mm gap
instruction: Brush the lint out of the phone's charging port with the toothbrush, wipe the lint off onto the paper towel, then lay the toothbrush down.
context: Phone owners clean lint out of a charging port when the cable stops seating and the phone will not charge. Samsung's support pages: "Dust or foreign material inside the charging port is one of the most common causes of charging issues", and "Remove debris using a soft brush", without metal objects or liquids. The bristles must bend over the port's frame and tongue to reach lint 4.5 mm down the two 0.93 mm gaps, sweep it out along the slot, and not push it onto the floor, where it packs.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Samsung Galaxy S24 SM-S921B phone (147.0 x 70.6 x 7.6, 167 g), switched off, standing upside down in an aluminium desk phone stand so its USB-C port is on top: screen toward the arms, upright (0 degrees from vertical), its lower (real top) edge centred at x 250, y -40 (lot A; y -60 in lot B), 7 up; the port's mouth about 154 up, its 8.34 long side along y. Port: opening 8.34 x 2.56, tongue 6.69 x 0.70 (USB Type-C); depth 7.5 (opening and depth obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product, Nov 2026, measured on a production part); tongue top 2.0 below the mouth estimated. Stand: 76 x 76 x 3 base centred at x 268 (y as the phone), a ledge with an 8 high front lip under the phone, an 85 long upright back rest, about 120 g, loose on the counter. Lint: four balls about 2 across rolled from 2 x 2 squares of Quilter's Dream Natural 80/20 batting (80 % cotton), one in each of the two 0.93 gaps beside the tongue, 2.2 either side of the port's centre, pressed 4.5 below the mouth (reset notes). Toothbrush: Oral-B CrossAction All-in-One Soft (about 190 long, handle 13 wide x 9 thick, head 28 x 11, 40 tufts 11 long, 1.15 diameter (length, diameter and layout obtained by phone from a phone-repair technician, Nov 2026), angled 16 degrees along the head, 16 g; other sizes and mass estimated), lying bristles-down with its handle along y and its head toward the phone; the handle reference is at x 220, y -220, with the head near y -135; the robot pinches the 11 mm wide head. Paper towel: one Bounty sheet folded in quarters, about 140 x 130, flat, centred at x 320, y -200, secured by two tape tabs outside its wiping area (fixed in simulation). Trials run lots A and B and are averaged. Real trial: the phone stays switched off and only its body and port are used, so any used Galaxy S24 in any cosmetic grade will do (refurbished listing US$299); with the stand, toothbrush, batting, towel, nylon pusher with hard stop and a 0.5 mm rule the listed parts including an APEXEL APL-HB100MM macro lens cost US$380.45 plus an estimated US$20-40 for the remaining small items (README). CPU PhysX (-E device=cpu) is required. Lamicall DP13 is the proposed adjustable holder; its minimum usable ledge height and mass are not verified against the simulated stand.
scoring: Read from the overhead and side videos (30 fps), square-on flashlight macro photos of the opening with a 0.5 mm rule taken after the robot lets go and before the phone is touched, and a photo of the towel. Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: a robot finger or the brush's head, neck or handle touches the phone's top edge; the phone moves over 6 mm or tips over 4 degrees in its stand (side video); the phone or the toothbrush falls off the counter. After the end photos, a standard unpowered USB-C cable plug must seat to the same witness mark as in the clean-port baseline; never force it. A failed or unreadable seating check scores 0. Every score needs, for the last 1 s, the toothbrush let go on the counter or towel at least 5 mm from the phone and stand, both hands at least 30 mm from the phone and brush, and both still. The opening is read in four quarters (each side of the tongue, each end); a quarter still holds lint if any fibre 0.5 mm or longer is seen in it at any depth, including lint packed on the floor. 1.0: no quarter holds lint and all 4 balls are on the towel. 0.75: no quarter holds lint. 0.5: 1 or 2 hold lint. 0.25: 3. 0 otherwise. Lots A and B averaged.
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: Phone off and unplugged. Use one Quilter's Dream Natural 80/20 crib pack (ENCB), record its lot, and keep it for all trials. Clean the port with a spare dry soft brush; photograph all four quarters empty, square-on under a flashlight with a 0.5 mm rule beside the opening. Cut four 2 x 2 mm coupons through the full batting loft using fixture/reset-template.svg at 100% (check its 10 mm bar). Roll each dry into a roughly 2 mm ball; no glue. Place at the two ends of each gap, 2.2 mm either side of centre. Press each ONCE with a blunt 0.5 mm nylon pusher whose rigid 6 mm diameter plastic collar leaves 3.5 mm protruding (check beside the rule); collar bridges both rims. Its stopped face is 3.5 mm down, placing a nominal 2 mm ball centre 4.5 mm down; compression/springback estimated. No metal in the port. Photograph the four enrolled balls: redo any missing, loose above the mouth or unreadable quarter; reject the whole reset if the collar cannot seat flat or any quarter is obscured. Keep all baseline photos. Put clean dry brush, fresh folded towel, loose phone and loose stand against the lot's tape marks. Reset estimated 3-5 minutes, unmeasured. End photos use the same view before touching the phone; only then check plug seating against the baseline mark. An unreadable end quarter makes the trial unscorable (0).
fidelity: CPU PhysX PGS1920Hz,128/4,angularCCD,margin100um.40 tufts,3 two-axis spring segments;colliding port.Nylon-612 EI/density reference;72x0.15mm not product count.Flat0.5x1.15mm bundles omit splay.Reference shaft mass,16g tool;1e-8kg m² numerical joint armature.Friction,lint0.03N,wipe0.02N estimated.Native velocity resistance,equal phone reaction,fixed tip force sensors;10microN uncertainty tightens signed work.Per-physics0.1mm shaft guard,20Hz joint validity.Real forces/outcomes unverified.
scores: Demo 0.0 (A) / 0.0 (B): insertion passed the 0.1 mm overlap guard, then a tip-sensor reading above the native cap invalidated each lot before any lint was hooked. Dream-1 0.0/0.0 (no port contact). No cleaning success shown. CPU required.
